_README: SOURCE OF TRUTH for the app's Model Analysis tab. Do NOT hand-edit the per-model error numbers in production — regenerate this file by running `python model/export_metrics.py` ON THE CLUSTER (where the dataset lives) after you retrain. The app reads this file and computes avoidable-bias/variance live, so: retrain -> export_metrics.py -> commit -> reboot app -> tab updates automatically.

task.name: Door-Hanging Safety Classifier
task.description: Binary image classification: is a passenger hanging on the door of a bus/leguna (unsafe) or not (safe)?
task.split: 70/15/15 stratified (train 269 / val 58 / test 58). NOTE: transfer models (ResNet50/ConvNeXt/EfficientNet) were retrained on train+val for deployment, so their val is not held out — see methodology_note.
task.primary_metric_note: Because data is imbalanced 2.9:1, watch UNSAFE-RECALL (catching violations), not just accuracy. A 'always safe' model already scores 74.5% accuracy while catching 0 violations.

human_level.definition: Careful expert reviewing the full-resolution image (can zoom). Used as the Bayes-error proxy.
human_level.why_not_zero: Irreducible error is above 0: the annotations themselves contain mistakes (e.g. legua/IMG_3719 is an empty parked leguna labelled 'unsafe'), and some unsafe hangers occupy only 1-8% of a cluttered frame. Even expert humans miss/dispute these.
human_level.how_to_measure: Have 2-3 teammates label a 40-50 image blind sample (run `python model/export_metrics.py --hlp-sample 50`); the inter-annotator disagreement rate is your empirical human-level error. Update this field with the result.

error_analysis.summary: Of 83 unsafe images, only ~6 score below 0.5 confidence. The biggest, cheapest win is fixing mislabelled images (~11-13), NOT more modelling — AUC plateaued at ~0.93 across 6+ architectures, the signature of a data ceiling.

categories.ceiling: Recovers recall + raises the usable threshold

diagnosis.verdict: Data-limited (variance-limited), NOT bias-limited — now confirmed by measured train vs held-out error.
diagnosis.reasoning: Every model shows near-zero avoidable bias (train error <= human ~4%) but a large train->held-out gap. Deep transfer nets fit training almost perfectly (~0% train) yet generalize at ~14-19% on the held-out test (5-fold CV corroborates ~9-10%); classical HOG models overfit too (SVM 1.9% train -> 15.5% val). Bigger models do not help — the signature of a variance/data ceiling, matching the AUC ~0.93 plateau across 6+ architectures.
next_actions: Collect more clear UNSAFE images (currently only 98) — the highest-return fix for a variance-limited model.
Fix the ~10-13 mislabelled images surfaced by the label audit.
Keep current regularisation/augmentation (already strong); do NOT just scale up model size.
Deploy the high-recall operating point behind a human-review queue rather than chasing accuracy.
diagnosis.note_classical_vs_deep: CORRECTION from measured data: the classical HOG models are NOT bias-limited (underfitting) as first assumed — they OVERFIT (low train, high val error), i.e. variance-limited like the deep nets. So the whole model zoo sits in the high-variance regime, which is why more/cleaner data is the lever, not architecture.
diagnosis.methodology_note: Held-out error = val by default. ResNet50/ConvNeXt/EfficientNet were retrained on train+val (train_cv.py), so their val error is contaminated; those use TEST as the held-out instead (flagged in the table). Train error is measured on ORIGINAL un-augmented images at the balanced (argmax) threshold, per standard bias/variance practice (Ng, Machine Learning Yearning; arXiv:2105.13343).
